result:
Done. PR #153 is ready, labelled, mergeable, and no longer in draft.

## What the previous attempt left, and why

Attempt 2 resolved the `fold.sh` conflict **correctly** — and then ended between `git commit` and `git push`. `origin/lane/draftstrand` was still at the pre-merge head, and `NOTES.md` (46 lines describing that merge, in the past tense) was sitting uncommitted. From inside the worktree everything looked finished; from GitHub nothing had happened. That's the same defect as attempt 1 one step later: the omitted action was the last one, and the only one with no actor behind it.

## What I did

1. Pushed attempt 2's resolution **first, on its own** — the missing step went out before anything else could go wrong.
2. Merged the 29 newer master commits. **Clean** — none of them touches any of this lane's six files. GitHub confirms `mergeable: MERGEABLE`; `needs-rebase` removed, `harness` and `fold-ready` added, PR non-draft.

## The blocker I found — it isn't mine, and I measured that rather than asserting it

Selftest on my head: 586 passed, **10 failed**. Those failures are in the fold area and this lane touches `fold.sh`, so they looked like mine. They aren't:

| tree | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| pristine `origin/master` @ `732b97e2df` | 516 | **10** |
| `lane/draftstrand` @ `76b2f486a0` | 586 | **10** |

The sorted `FAIL` lines `diff` **empty**. Master's own selftest has been red on every commit since `4eb641e777` (15:03Z), green on the two before.

**Mechanism — two lanes green apart, red together.** #137 `branchprune` added `prune_branch` (deletes the lane ref after a fold). #145 `foldregress` added a fixture that creates `lane/foldreg` once and restores it by pushing it. The fixture drives the *real* `fold.sh`, so its first folding tick now deletes the branch it reuses. Each PR was green on its own head because #145's base predated #137's fold — no per-PR gate can see this.

I verified the fix rather than guessing: restoring the ref in `fr_reset` takes pristine master to **526 passed, 0 failed**. I did **not** apply it here — `selftest.d/86-fold-regressed.sh` isn't on this PR's `Files:` line and the handback said not to extend the work. The diagnosis and tested patch are in a `[lane.draftstrand] blocked:` comment. A `lane/selftest86` worktree already sits at current master with no branch yet, so the board likely dispatched this already; I flagged it so nobody starts a second lane on it.

## Two caveats you should weigh

- **CI on #153 is RED and will stay red while master is red.** I set `fold-ready` anyway, knowingly: `fold.sh` re-gates on `ci_green` itself, so it can't cause a bad fold, but it means #153 folds automatically once master is repaired — no fourth lane session. Leaving it unlabelled would have made it a PR with no actor, which is the defect this lane exists to remove.
- **`preflight.sh --allow-tracker` fails one gate**: `coverage`, because issue **#164** has neither a lane nor a `blocked_on` in `territory.toml` on `origin/board` — a file this lane is forbidden to edit. Every other gate passes.

So two of the three gates this session had to clear were already failing before it started, for unrelated reasons, on files outside its grant. The harness currently cannot fold *anything* until fragment 86 is fixed — a jam worse than the stranded drafts this lane was dispatched for.
